title: Multiplex PCR for the Identification of the Salmonid Pathogen Tenacibaculum finnmarkense and Discrimination of the Finnmarkense and Ulcerans Genomovars
content:
ABSTRACT

Tenacibaculum finnmarkense is an important pathogen of farmed salmon in Norway and Chile, comprising the finnmarkense and ulcerans genomovars. This study aimed to develop a multiplex PCR (mPCR) assay for species-specific identification of T. finnmarkense and discrimination between its two genomovars using comparative genomics. Comparative pan-genome analysis of 127 genomes identified genomic regions suitable for species- and genomovar-level discrimination. A gene encoding a LuxR-family protein was selected for species-level identification, generating a 313-bp amplicon. For genomovar discrimination, a gene encoding a protein of unknown function was selected for the finnmarkense genomovar, whereas a TroA-family protein-encoding gene was selected for the ulcerans genomovar, generating 659-bp and 427-bp amplicons, respectively. The assay was validated using DNA from 34 T. finnmarkense isolates and 28 non-target bacterial pathogens, with no non-specific amplification observed. Using pure bacterial suspensions, detection limits were 2.4 ± 2.83 × 106 CFU/mL for T. finnmarkense genomovar finnmarkense HFJ and 2.8 ± 3.5 × 106 CFU/mL for the ulcerans genomovar LBP5. The assay specifically identified T. finnmarkense and discriminated between its two genomovars from pure bacterial cultures. However, its relatively high detection limits and validation using pure bacterial suspensions do not support direct detection from fish tissues. The assay therefore provides a rapid molecular alternative for the identification and genomovar assignment of cultured T. finnmarkense isolates recovered from suspected cases of tenacibaculosis.
